title: Research: bit E8 decoder witness and 9/17 pairing-cost floor
body:
Research note / scoped decoder construction and lower bound. **No new kappa or hosted supplier.**

In the fixed bit label-decoder model on real E8, priced by rational pairing
rank under [PR 446](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/446)'s inherited copy premise, nine orthogonal punctured root pairs
give an exact decoder of cost **54 on 102 ports**. A written argument supported
by exact finite censuses bounds **cst/v >= 9/17** for every puncture of at most
25 lines and any number of label terms. Equality occurs at 18 punctures; the
package gives explicit nine-term witnesses for every p=0..25.

Keeping the selected [PR 589](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/589) reader basis fixed, one source dual is a root that
can be deleted to produce a P110 decoder with cost 62. A scope control changes
that basis and obtains two cost-6 terms but costs 68 overall. These are
algebraic decoders only. The fixed R439 inventory
passes the aggregate capacity screen at v=110, whereas v=102 has only 408
slots; no actual owner map, asymmetric copy, frame/restoration schedule or
complete changed-supplier invoice is built.

Only `research/bit-orthogonal-pair-decoders/` is added. Exact base:
`2921874911956718fcaaaf9396fe8267b3cfa9f0`. Selected pointers, `upstream/` and
all existing packages remain unchanged. Source pins, literal witness,
deterministic receipt, proof, controls and validation are included.

At submission upstream had advanced to
`abdc6a7002abdbcd9e21bfc5e1a795784deacfdf`; all seven pinned executable/data
inputs remain byte-identical and [PR 942](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/942) remains selected. The research branch
keeps its exact recorded base rather than importing unrelated concurrent work.

One reproducible command, Python 3.10+ and standard library only:

```sh
python3 -I -B research/bit-orthogonal-pair-decoders/test_package.py
```

This runs the primary and a separate implementation, compares regenerated
receipt bytes, and tests corruption rejection. The primary refuses `-O`
because the unchanged pinned pricing engines use assertions. Local execution
on CPython 3.12.14 and 3.13.15 and selected-source integrity checks are recorded
in `VALIDATION.md`; no whole-repository suite or hosted CI pass is claimed.

[PR 620](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/620) identified the orthogonal-pair mechanism; [PR 757](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/757) and [PR 761](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/761) certify the
fixed P111 floor; [PR 595](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/595) named the unrealised 54/102 unit. This contribution adds
a literal exact decoder and a puncture-independent rational pairing-cost
bound, not priority for those predecessor observations. [PR 968](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/968) is the distinct
complex frame-pair analogue, with a different cost. Recent [PR 1020](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1020) uses complex
F2 label ranks at 26 punctures and [PR 1008](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1008) uses fixed-P111 tensor shears; neither
duplicates this scope. The immediate refresh through [PR 1081](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1081) also found [PR 1077](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1077)'s
complex-coefficient extension of [PR 968](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/968), another distinct eight-term model.
Credit and exact source heads are retained in
`NOTICE.md` and `SOURCES.json`.

Inherited parabolic coverage, copy interpretation, compiler, hosting,
precision/tape and analytic obligations remain explicit. The written argument
and finite replay are not proof-assistant verification of multiplication or
independent human review. Prepared for @navinor with substantial
AI assistance through OpenCode; resumed review/packaging used GPT-6.1 Sol
(OpenAI). Apache-2.0. Structural-decoder track, OS assignment seed 40; no pinned
coordination issue existed, so the claim is local.
